title: Ligaments of the lumbar vertebral column (right lateral)
attribution: 3D anatomy from Z-Anatomy, built on BodyParts3D (CC BY-SA). Rendered in Blender; surface detail added with an image model.

rows: Attachments
A broad band down the front of the vertebral bodies and intervertebral discs, from the base of the skull and the atlas to the pelvic surface of the sacrum.
Function
Limits extension of the vertebral column and supports the front of the intervertebral discs.
hy: It can be stretched or torn in a hyperextension (whiplash) injury of the neck.

rows: Attachments
Join the spinous processes of neighboring vertebrae, from the root of each process to its tip.
Function
Limit flexion of the vertebral column.
Attachments
Tips of the spinous processes from C7 to the sacrum. Above C7 it continues as the ligamentum nuchae.
Function
Limits flexion of the vertebral column.
hy: The first ligament the needle passes in a midline lumbar puncture: supraspinous ligament, interspinous ligament, ligamentum flavum, epidural space, dura mater, arachnoid mater.

rows: Location
Between the bodies of neighboring vertebrae from C2 and C3 down to L5 and S1. There is none between the atlas and the axis.
Parts
An outer ring of fibrocartilage, the anulus fibrosus, around a gel-like center, the nucleus pulposus.
Function
Bear weight, absorb shock, and allow movement between the vertebrae.
hy: In a herniated disc the nucleus pulposus bulges through the anulus, usually posterolaterally. It is most common at L4 to L5 and L5 to S1 and usually compresses the nerve root numbered for the vertebra below (L5 at an L4 to L5 disc).
The nucleus pulposus is a remnant of the notochord.

rows: Location
Uppermost of the five lumbar vertebrae, below the twelfth thoracic vertebra. The spinal cord usually ends at about this level (L1 to L2) in adults.
Articulates with
T12 above and L2 below, through the intervertebral discs and the facet joints.
Features
Large kidney-shaped body and a short, thick spinous process; like all lumbar vertebrae it has no facets for ribs and no foramina in its transverse processes.
Location
Second of the five lumbar vertebrae.
Articulates with
L1 above and L3 below, through the intervertebral discs and the facet joints.
Features
Large body with thick pedicles and laminae; its articular facets face medially and laterally, which allows flexion and extension but little rotation.
Location
Middle lumbar vertebra, at the peak of the forward curve of the lumbar spine.
Articulates with
L2 above and L4 below, through the intervertebral discs and the facet joints.
Features
Large body; its transverse processes are the longest of the lumbar vertebrae.
Location
Fourth lumbar vertebra. A line joining the highest points of the iliac crests crosses its spinous process or the space between L4 and L5.
Articulates with
L3 above and L5 below, through the intervertebral discs and the facet joints.
Features
Large body and a thick, blunt spinous process.
Location
Lowest and largest lumbar vertebra, resting on the base of the sacrum.
Articulates with
L4 above and the sacrum below.
Features
Its body is taller in front than behind, and its stout transverse processes give attachment to the iliolumbar ligaments.
hy: A defect of the pars interarticularis (spondylolysis) is most common at L5 and can let the body of L5 slip forward on the sacrum (spondylolisthesis).
